key_insight: VETime fuses vision foundation models with temporal alignment to get the best of both worlds: vision-based global context and 1D temporal pointwise localization, enabling zero-shot detection of both short-term (point) and long-range (context) anomalies.
problem_solved: Addresses the fundamental trade-off in TSAD where 1D temporal models localize points but miss global context, while 2D vision models capture global patterns but lack fine-grained temporal alignment and pointwise accuracy—plus the need for zero-shot (label-free) anomaly detection.
method: Translate time series into vision-friendly representations and leverage pretrained vision foundation models to capture global contextual patterns without task-specific labels.
Introduce a temporal-alignment / fusion module that preserves fine-grained, pointwise temporal information while integrating vision-derived global embeddings.
Produce anomaly scores in a zero-shot manner by comparing aligned temporal features and vision-global context to detect both point and context anomalies without supervised training.
impact: VETime enables practitioners to detect diverse anomaly types (instantaneous spikes and long-range contextual shifts) without labeled anomalies, improving monitoring pipelines and lowering annotation cost while leveraging powerful pretrained vision models.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: time-series → image encoding → vision encoder + temporal-alignment module → anomaly scoring (clear flow of information)
Before/after example: raw time series with overlaid heatmap showing improved pointwise localization and contextual anomaly detection

paper_title: VETime: Vision Enhanced Zero-Shot Time Series Anomaly Detection
paper_authors: Yingyuan Yang, Tian Lan, Yifei Gao, Yimeng Lu, Wenjun He
